newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish court halts Mostostal mast project.
newsitem.headline: Polish court halts Mostostal mast project.

text.p: Poland's Supreme Administrative Court has halted plans by state-owned telecommunications firm TPSA to build the world's tallest radio and television mast -- a contract held by construction firm Mostostal Zabrze SA.
Saturday's Gazeta Wyborcza newspaper said the Lodz court's unexpected decision was not subject to appeal and would at the least mean a major delay in the 25-million-zloty project.
Mostostal last year won the contract to build the 646-metre mast near Gabin, central Poland, replacing one that collapsed in 1991, and said it had beaten off several European firms to get the job.
But local residents fought the scheme, arguing that the electromagnetic waves from the mast could harm their health.
The court ruled on Friday that the project infringed new building regulations and had not been properly prepared.

The ruling is also a blow to public Polish Radio, which had planned to transmit long wave broadcasts of its main First Programme from the mast. The programme is now broadcast over much of the country from another mast which needs renovation.
Polish Radio and TPSA (Telekomunikacja Polska SA) told Gazeta Wyborcza they would submit a new application.

"We will have to arrange this matter again from the beginning. It is hard to say how long this will delay construction," the paper quoted Polish Radio's lawyer Wieslaw Johann as saying. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
